subject: Agriculture
title: Earthworms as Engineers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Earthworms as Engineers usable.

hook.text: Charles Darwin spent 40 years studying earthworms. He called them the most important animals in history.

buildup.text: Earthworms eat dead plant matter and soil, digesting it into nutrient-rich castings—nature's best fertilizer.

discovery.text: Their tunnels aerate the soil and create channels for water to infiltrate instead of running off.

twist.text: A healthy field may have over a million earthworms per acre, moving 20 tons of soil per year.

climax.text: Pesticides and deep plowing kill earthworms. Losing them means losing free soil maintenance.

punchline.text: The humblest farmer works underground, for free.

quiz.question: Why did Darwin consider earthworms so important?
options: They aerate soil, recycle nutrients, and move tons of earth yearly
